method.rdap: Anonymous HTTPS GET to rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/{domain}; verified TLS and public pinned address, no redirects; 128 KiB cap and 11 s hard process deadline.
method.doh: DNS A/AAAA only over anonymous RFC8484 HTTPS POST to dns.alidns.com and doh.pub; verified TLS and public pinned resolver address; no redirects; 64 KiB cap and 11 s hard process deadline.
method.rate: At most two concurrent request workers and at least 0.4 seconds between starts; two rounds.
method.privacy: No source host connection, credential, RDAP body, registration/registrant data, concrete IP, CNAME or raw DNS answer saved.

method_precision: The 0.4 second limiter applies to worker launch scheduling; recorded network start times can differ slightly because process startup varies.
limitations: DNS responses and RDAP status are time-sensitive; missing DNS is not proof of domain deletion or permanent source failure.
A registered RDAP domain object does not imply the old host resolves or the source works.
Both DoH services share this client/network path; DNSSEC AD is reported but not validated locally.
Raw answers were deliberately not retained; response hashes cannot be independently reconstructed from this redacted draft.
Selected source records are from a local catalog snapshot, not evidence of installation or user settings.
The two rounds are separated by tens of seconds and can reuse resolver caches; they do not constitute independent networks or regions.
An RDAP 404 with empty body supplies no RDAP errorCode or explanation; it does not establish prior deletion or future status.
The five matching RDAP domain objects are registered-domain counterexamples, not evidence that old subdomains or rules work.
The transient build/ collector scripts and draft are not committed; their SHA-256 values cannot be checked in a fresh checkout.
Historical response bytes were not saved; DNS response hashes and observed parsing cannot be independently regenerated from redacted metadata.
Recomputing historical source associations requires Git and the referenced ledger object; shallow clones or source archives may omit it.
